text:
TBL had the better of the game and won it, but the margin was thinner than the scoreboard suggests. John Carlson turned two shots with a 3% and an 11% chance of scoring into goals, the first one 36 seconds after Anthony Cirelli's tip-in, and TBL led 2-0 before the first period was seven minutes old. Cirelli's goal was only an 8% look, so the early lead owed plenty to finishing. The chances still favored TBL in that period, 1.34 expected goals to 0.61.

MIN spent the rest of the night chasing. Quinn Hughes cut it to 2-1 early in the second, but Carlson answered on the power play, a slap shot at 4:55, to make it 3-1. Blake Coleman scored on a MIN power play at 14:01 to make it 3-2, and that was the last goal. MIN outchanced TBL in the second, 1.38 to 1.10, and again in the third by a hair, 1.07 to 1.05, without finding the equalizer. Marcus Foligno had the best look of the night, a 23% chance in the second period that missed the net.

Over the full game TBL held a modest edge, 3.49 expected goals to 3.06, and deserved to win 57% of the time. Dennis Hildeby saved 1.06 goals more than expected for TBL. Carlson put nine shots on goal and was named first star. Hughes played 32:36 for MIN and finished with a goal and an assist, but the early deficit was too much to erase.
